objective: Proof and computation. A crossing knot made of two near points and one far point is generated when a route exists: one port separates it, or a pair of the gluing line's points is forced by the near pair on one side and covered by the far point's excluded block on the other, with a tie or a one-step near knot at the near end. Prove that a route generates the knot, and test on Fano planes attached at a point of plane pieces, with the removal inside the handle, whether every knot without a route is new and every new knot lacks one. The criterion reads the plane piece only through the transfer between the handle's ports and the gluing line.
status: Proved by HALO-FORCING-20261103-001A-P001: a three-point crossing knot at a gluing line is generated when it has a route (one point of the line separates, or a pair of the line's points is fixed by the near pair and covered by the far point's excluded block, with a tie or a one-step near knot at the near end). Computed converse: with the Fano plane attached at a point of five plane pieces and the removal inside it, the new knots are exactly the candidates with a handle point and no route (1,500 new; 59,984 routed candidate instances, none new), and creation is a function of the transfer between the handle's ports and the gluing line
title: The route criterion
